survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note does not use student-level ILSA microdata or administer an assessment; it provides a descriptive overview of governance and expenditure arrangements in New Zealand’s adult skills system. As a result, there is no sampling frame for students, no complex survey design, and no application of student/sampling weights (e.g., W_FSTUWT, TOTWGT) or replicate-weight methods (e.g., BRR/jackknife). The tables describe institutional responsibilities and governance levels rather than statistical estimation from survey responses. Therefore, plausible values (PV) and missing-data handling are not part of the analysis pipeline in this document.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a governance and policy description of adult skills system institutions, not an empirical analysis predicting cognitive achievement outcomes from ILSA/PV-based test scores. Because there is no student-level assessment dataset with plausible values and no statistical model that would require PV combination, PV handling is not applicable. Missing-data handling is also not reported because no microdata-based estimation is conducted in this country note.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No student-level sample is used. The note is based on documentary sources and OECD compilation of governance responsibilities and expenditure structure for New Zealand.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD country note summarizes how New Zealand’s adult skills system is governed across national, regional, and local levels. It reports that the system is relatively centralised: the national government sets the legislative framework and allocates funding, while implementation and delivery occur through national agencies and subnational structures. The note details responsibilities for vocational education and training (VET), adult and community education (ACE), and active labour market policies (ALMPs), including the roles of Te Pūkenga, the Tertiary Education Commission, the New Zealand Qualifications Authority, and the Ministry of Social Development’s Public Employment Service. It also describes ongoing VET reforms expected to take effect from 1 January 2026 and how these reforms aim to strengthen regional decision-making and industry-led standards-setting. No assessment instruments, student outcomes, or ML-based predictive models are analysed; the document is descriptive and policy-oriented rather than empirical.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction contains many nulls because the document is not an empirical large-scale assessment or ML study: it is a descriptive OECD country note on governance structures. There is no student sample, no ILSA/PISA/TIMSS/PIRLS-style assessment dataset, and no statistical modelling that would generate predictive targets, performance metrics, or ML algorithms. Consequently, fields such as total_students, countries-by-sample-size, PV handling, missing-data handling, and main_findings are not applicable to the document’s purpose.
